units.translation: Thus in M προσηλούμενον [being nailed to], not προσελούμενον, as is written in some copies, where the readings fluctuate between the two writings. The correct reading πρου-σελοῦμεν is in Arist. Ran. 730 in the Ravenna manuscript, in the Venetian and others προσελοῦμεν
Stobaeus Flor. 43, 28 προυγελοῦμεν [we mock beforehand], as

Hesychius προυγελεῖν [to mock beforehand]: προπηλακίζειν [to insult], ὑβρίζειν [to outrage]. The meaning of the verb is clear, but the origin is uncertain, about which there are various opinions of both ancient and recent grammarians, on which see Thes. vol. 6 p. 2084, Hermann in his note on the verse of Aeschylus, Clemm in Rit.
having been brought forward in oracles
having fled from the black-horsed sacred night's milking-time
Loxias is the prophet of his father Zeus
the heart, anticipating the tongue, would pour out these things
Thus corrected, which is in M ἄνασσ᾽ Ογκα προ [queen Onca, before] (πρό [before] with accent by a later hand) πόλεως ἑπτάπυλον [of the seven-gated city]: see Praef. ed. Lips. quintae p. LB.
and you, blessed queen Onca, willingly guard the seven-gated seat of the city
and whoever willingly shouts victory songs to Zeus will attain complete wisdom
send help willingly to the children for victory
I willingly do these things for these citizens
I rejoice that these things are willingly accomplished for my land
may Zeus the protector look willingly upon our expedition
Thus corrected, which is in M ἄνασσ᾽ Ογκα προ [queen Onca, before] (πρό [before] with accent by a later hand) πόλεως ἑπτάπυλον [of the seven-gated city]: see Praef. ed. Lips. quintae p. LB
and may a propitious god watch over you
may he forgive and stand by propitiously
hear me with a propitious heart
[To the similarity of this verse I composed a verse which is found
Sept. 195. about which see προσαιθρίζω [to expose to the air] will be said.]
Προ-φωνῶν τὰ τῶν πέλας [proclaiming the affairs of neighbors]
thus Canterus for πρόφρων ὤν [being propitious]
he proclaims this word to all the ship-captains
therefore I proclaim to all to keep quiet
proclaiming the great wrath of Zeus the suppliant
To the similarity of this verse I composed a verse which is found
Sept. 195. about which see προσαιθρίζω [to expose to the air] will be said
